text:
mika: FYI I spun up kestrel-embed (fp16 -> int8 per-channel) on staging and ran the smoke onboarding on named-entity-heavy slices (wiki-entities). Seeing a cluster-level recall drop concentrated on short entity queries (names, dates).

mika: quick numbers (round-trip):

fp16: R@1 0.78 | R@5 0.92 | R@10 0.96
int8-pc: R@1 0.71 | R@5 0.87 | R@10 0.91

devin: Can you share the exact eval command + dataset split? Also whether you enabled whitening or any ad-hoc centering?

mika: Command: `embed_eval --model kestrel-embed --repr int8-pc --dataset wiki-entities --k 1,5,10 --out /tmp/kestrel_int8.json`
No whitening changes, default normalize=True. I used the entity-slice (queries primarily 3-8 tokens).

rachel: Two quick hypotheses: 1) quant calibration not representative for infrequent tokens (proper nouns), 2) pooling sensitivity: short named entities often rely on a few token dims that might be damped by per-channel scaling.

devin: Dump 10 failure cases (query + expected doc + top-1) and run `--normalize false` paired eval to see magnitude vs direction issues. Also compare L2 norm histograms for queries and docs separately.

mika: Pasted 2 examples from failures.json:
1) query: "Ada Lovelace"
expected: "ada lovelace biography"
actual: "history of computing"

2) query: "Treaty of Versailles 1919"
expected: "treaty of versailles text"
actual: "postwar treaties overview"

ci-bot: [ci] nightly-embed-scan flagged this model on entity-slice at 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z. Job: https://ci.redwood/embeds/4478908765

rachel: Also try int8-pt (per-tensor) and a per-channel asymmetric variant. Sometimes asymmetric quant preserves tail activation distributions for rare tokens.

devin: Suggest running small calibration re-run sampled from the entity slice (5-20k examples) and re-exporting quant tables. Command: `tools/quant_calibrate.py --model kestrel-embed --repr int8-pc --calib-sample data/wiki-entities-calib.json --seed 42 --out calibs/kestrel_pc_calib.npz`

mika: I'll run: int8-pt, int8-pc-asym, and fp16 paired evals, plus `--normalize false` runs. Then I'll produce: 1) paired cosine delta histogram, 2) L2 norm boxplots by token-length, 3) UMAP of 3k entity queries to inspect cluster shifts.

rachel: Good. If we see large cosine deltas concentrated in a few dims, run PCA on pre-pool token features to inspect explained variance collapse. If asym per-channel helps, we can adopt asym for entity-sensitive builds.
